use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader};

// Define a function to read the graph edge list and build an adjacency list
fn read_graph(filename: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let file = File::open(filename).unwrap();
    let reader = BufReader::new(file);
    let mut graph: HashMap<String, Vec<String>> = HashMap::new();
    for line in reader.lines() {
        let line = line.unwrap();
        let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split(',').collect();
        if parts[0] != "source_node" {
            let source_node = parts[0].to_string();
            let target_node = parts[1].to_string();
            graph.entry(source_node).or_insert(Vec::new()).push(target_node);
        }
    }
    graph
}

// Define a function to perform a BFS traversal
fn bfs(graph: &HashMap<String, Vec<String>>, start_node: &str, target_node: &str) -> i32 {
    let mut queue: VecDeque<(String, i32)> = VecDeque::new();
    let mut visited: HashMap<String, bool> = HashMap::new();
    queue.push_back((start_node.to_string(), 0));
    while let Some((node, distance)) = queue.pop_front() {
        if node == target_node {
            return distance;
        }
        if visited.contains_key(&node) {
            continue;
        }
        visited.insert(node.clone(), true);
        if let Some(neighbors) = graph.get(&node) {
            for neighbor in neighbors {
                queue.push_back((neighbor.clone(), distance + 1));
            }
        }
    }
    -1
}
